hook: Dust lag around small black holes grows with luminosity at a slope of 0.47, just under the 0.5 expected.
summary: Dust around growing black holes echoes their optical flicker in infrared light, and the delay gives the dust distance. Using ZTF and WISE data for 65 low-mass active galactic nuclei, the authors extend the radius-luminosity relation over nearly seven orders of magnitude. The slightly shallow slope may reflect shadowing by slim disks or imperfect luminosity proxies. Both explanations are suggested, not tested directly.
title: Dust Reverberation Mapping of Low-Mass Active Galactic Nuclei
